clue.text: Growing concern following beastly takeover

parts.note: a growing concern is a place where crops grow, and the beastly takeover is the livestock seizing power in Orwell's fable

explanation.surface: A business on the up after an aggressive acquisition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Growing concern' looks like a thriving business but means a place for raising crops; the 'beastly takeover' is the revolt of the animals in George Orwell's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Orwell's satirical novel tells of livestock overthrowing their human owner and running the holding themselves.

clue.text: A fish or seaweed extract

parts.note: the gar is a long-snouted fish

explanation.surface: A menu choice between fish or a jelly made from seaweed.
explanation.definitionFit: This jelly, used in labs and cooking, is obtained from red algae.

clue.text: Once forced to join up, had real impact

definitions.meaning: in the past men were seized by press gangs and forced into the navy
made a strong impression on someone

explanation.surface: A conscripted man made his mark in the service.
explanation.definitionFit: Press gangs once conscripted sailors by force; a person who has made a strong impression on another has also done this.

clue.text: The capital of a couple of hundred big guns

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so two of them
RA is the Royal Artillery, the army's big guns

explanation.surface: A city defended by two hundred artillery pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Accra is the capital city of Ghana.

clue.text: Make way

definitions.meaning: a manner or style of doing things

explanation.definitionFit: To fashion something is to make it, and 'in this fashion' means in this way or manner.

clue.text: Activists' new roster absorbing the unit

definitions.note: the definition is plural; the possessive 's is surface dressing

indicators.note: absorbing means the reworked letters take in another piece within them
new signals that the letters of roster are given a fresh arrangement

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one, a unit

explanation.surface: A campaign group's latest list of members includes one more person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' turns ROSTER into ROTERS, and 'absorbing' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Protesters who take to the streets in violent disorder are militant campaigners of a kind.

clue.text: Naval port

parts.note: port here is not a harbour but the side of a ship as sailors name it

explanation.surface: A harbour used by the navy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' looks like a harbour such as Portsmouth, but at sea port is the side on your left as you face the bow.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailors call the left-hand side of a vessel port, so in naval language the word means the opposite of right.

clue.text: Finding bearings after a time, get out

indicators.note: after places the compass letters behind the period of time

parts.note: an era is a period of time
SE, south-east, is a compass bearing

explanation.surface: A navigator, having got their bearings after a while, escapes.
explanation.definitionFit: To rub out a mark or get out a stain is to remove it entirely.

clue.text: Insures hides

explanation.surface: Someone buys a policy and lies low.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who buys an insurance policy obtains protection, and someone ducking into shelter from fire does the same thing physically.

clue.text: A form of support many a worker is wearing

parts.note: a bra is an undergarment that supports
D is the Roman numeral 500, a large number
the worker ant is the crossword's stock labourer

explanation.surface: An employee has a supportive undergarment on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wearing' looks like part of the picture of someone dressed, but it is the definition: an abrasive that wears surfaces away.
explanation.definitionFit: An abrasive material grinds and erodes surfaces, so it is something that wears others down.

clue.text: A spice endlessly used in savoury food

indicators.note: endlessly says the word spice loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A seasoning finds its way into a meaty dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' drops the last letter E from SPICE.
explanation.definitionFit: A clear jelly made from meat stock, used to set savoury dishes such as pies and terrines.

clue.text: Able perhaps to occupy jar cleaner

indicators.note: to occupy means the reworked letters sit inside the jolt word

parts.note: a jar is a jolt or shock

indicators.note: perhaps says the letters of Able may be arranged differently

explanation.surface: A capable person takes up residence in a clean pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jar' reads as a pot in the surface, but here it is a jolt; 'perhaps' is the anagram signal and 'to occupy' the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who cleaned and polished shoes for a living, once a common street trade.

clue.text: To put in reserve team after tea's unusual

indicators.note: after puts the team word behind the rearranged letters
unusual signals that the letters of tea's are put in an odd order

parts.note: the letters of tea's, with its s
a side is a team in sport

explanation.surface: A squad is benched once the refreshments are found to be strange.
explanation.walkthrough: 'team' joins the surface's picture of a squad, but it supplies a sports side; 'unusual' signals the anagram and 'after' places the team last.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep something back for later use, saving it as a reserve.

clue.text: Encourages when about to gamble

parts.note: a is an abbreviation for about, as with approximate dates
to bet is to gamble, here in the third person

explanation.surface: A punter is spurred on just as they are going to place a wager.
explanation.definitionFit: To abet is to help or egg on, usually in wrongdoing.

clue.text: Writer putting money into very large car — spacious

parts.note: OS stands for outsize, a clothing size
taken as written

indicators.note: into says the money letter goes inside the word for spacious

parts.note: wide means broad or spacious
L stands for pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: An author spends cash on a roomy limousine.
explanation.definitionFit: Irish playwright and wit who wrote The Importance of Being Earnest.

clue.text: Continue to offer support

definitions.meaning: keep going for a long time
bear the weight of or keep alive

explanation.surface: Keep on offering backing.
explanation.definitionFit: A note held for a long time is kept going, and a structure that bears a load holds it up.

clue.text: Irregular ban, moral though it may be

indicators.note: though it may be suggests the words ban and moral are only one possible order of these letters

explanation.surface: A prohibition is odd even if made on ethical grounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Something outside the usual pattern or norm is unusual or deviant.

clue.text: In Lewisham poor folk must share a washer

indicators.note: In says the letters are found inside the words Lewisham poor

explanation.surface: Poor people in a London district have to share a washing machine.
explanation.walkthrough: Lewisham is a district of south-east London; the run of letters sits across its end and the start of 'poor'.
explanation.definitionFit: A liquid soap for washing the hair, so something that cleans.

clue.text: Cast for the amusement of youngsters?

definitions.text: Cast for the amusement of youngsters?

parts.words: Cast for the amusement of youngsters?
parts.note: a cast is the company of actors performing a drama, here put on to entertain children

explanation.surface: Actors hired to entertain children.
explanation.walkthrough: The cast of a drama is its company of players; read the other way, this is a pre-school session where small children amuse themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: A supervised session where pre-school children meet to amuse themselves, and literally a band of players.

clue.text: Neat, and possibly rather slow

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters of neat and and may be rearranged

explanation.surface: A tidy and somewhat leisurely performer.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical tempo marking meaning at a moderately slow, walking pace.

clue.text: Dropping in the main

parts.note: the main is the open sea, and the dropping is the falling of its level

explanation.surface: A fall that happens for the most part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the main' looks like 'mostly', but 'the main' is an old word for the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The receding of the sea after high water, when its level falls.

clue.text: Note on evidence? Go over it again

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
a trace is a mark left behind, a piece of evidence

explanation.surface: A detective, writing a memo on the clues, reviews the case.
explanation.definitionFit: To follow the same path once more or review a sequence of events.

clue.text: He'd read about an auburn-haired woman

indicators.note: about signals that the letters of He'd read are moved around

explanation.surface: A man had been reading up on a red-haired lady.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman with reddish hair, such as auburn or ginger.

clue.text: A quarter say are doubtful

parts.note: W, west, is one of the four compass quarters
to aver is to state or say

explanation.surface: A quarter of people say they are unsure.
explanation.definitionFit: To hesitate or vacillate between choices.

clue.text: Opposing the top man a Latin can be articulate!

parts.note: v, versus, means against or opposing
OC is Officer Commanding, the man in charge

explanation.surface: Someone opposing the boss in Latin may speak out well.
explanation.definitionFit: Expressive in speech, outspoken, or relating to the voice.

clue.text: Jocular talk which could get naughty in time

parts.note: bad means misbehaving or naughty
taken as written
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Some playful chat that might turn rude in due course.
explanation.definitionFit: Light, teasing banter between people.

clue.text: Only the patient will attract her attention

definitions.text: Only the patient will attract her attention

parts.words: Only the patient will attract her attention
parts.note: the patient here is not someone calm but someone under medical care

explanation.surface: Patience is the only way to get her to notice you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'patient' reads as an adjective meaning calm, but it is a noun: the sick person on a ward.
explanation.definitionFit: A hospital carer attends to the sick people on the ward.

clue.text: The person working for some good cause regularly

indicators.note: some says only part of the words good cause regularly is taken

explanation.surface: A volunteer who often helps a charity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' looks like an alternate-letter signal, but the letters run straight across 'cause regularly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who uses or operates something, putting it to work for a purpose.

clue.text: Cook cut a liver in shreds. It's so beneficial

indicators.note: cook in the sense of fiddle or falsify, so the letters are tampered with
in shreds says the letters of cut a liver are torn up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A chef slices liver finely, which is good for you.
explanation.definitionFit: Profitable, yielding gain or advantage.

clue.text: Overcharges men on the board

definitions.meaning: cheats customers by charging too much

explanation.surface: Directors on the board charge too much.
explanation.definitionFit: To swindle someone is to fleece them, and the castles on a chessboard share the name.

clue.text: A girl using Spanish and French articles

parts.note: el is the Spanish word for the
la is French for the, feminine

explanation.surface: A girl uses words from two European languages.
explanation.definitionFit: A female first name, as in the jazz singer Fitzgerald.

clue.text: The custodian in control — one who is invariably calm

definitions.meaning: the senior warder or gamekeeper in charge
a person who never loses composure

explanation.surface: The chief guard never gets flustered.
explanation.definitionFit: A chief warden is the senior one, and someone who never panics keeps their cool, punningly holding on to their head.
